subject: Sprint safeguard: pricing endorsement request for delayed quant rollout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint safeguard: pricing endorsement request for delayed quant rollout

Team —

Quick context: DeltaHealth (P0 pilot, committed 2x dedicated nodes, public sector prospect) paused their launch last week after the quant rollout introduced a kernel-level regression that increased p99 inference latency by ~180ms for their long-sequence workloads. Product has since paused the rollout for that customer cohort; estimations from runtime say a targeted fix will land in the 2-week sprint after next.

Alex is asking for a short-term financial accommodation while they delay go-live — specifically a temporary pricing endorsement (discount or credit path) to cover the two-month launch slip. They’re sensitive about public-sector procurement windows and need something documented for their procurement team this week.

Ask to this thread: can we get an exec-level endorsement for a timeboxed, contingent rate accommodation that meets finance/legal guardrails? I sketched a proposition attached (proposed-rate-endorsement-term-sheet.xlsx) that says:
- 50% credit on committed baseline consumption for up to 2 billing cycles OR a 20% committed-rate for same period (customer chooses)
- Condition: acceptance into our Early Access remediation program + written acknowledgement that credit is one-time and conditional on acceptance of proposed rollout testing plan
- Roadmap milestone: fix merged to main and validated on DeltaHealth staging within 21 days of signoff

Notes: this is commercial-facing — we should keep the ask narrow, timeboxed, and tied to measurable milestones. If finance/legal say no credit, we could consider a temporary rate plan (short-term discounted rate) instead.

Attachments: DH-impact-summary-June2028.pdf (impact/schedule from customer), proposed-rate-endorsement-term-sheet.xlsx (commercial proposal)

Pls advise next steps and who needs to sign off. Customer timeline: procurement asks for documentation by Monday EOD.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifying Qs before I take this up the chain:
1) What is the expected ARR impact and is this a one-off or likely to set a precedent for other long-sequence pilots?
2) Can Legal/Finance live with the two options (credit vs temporary rate)? Which is cleaner from an accounting perspective?
3) Who in Product is validating the 21-day milestone and can commit to test windows?

If answers are quick I’ll prepare a short memo for Marissa with recommendation and risk points. I don’t want this to balloon into an open-ended concession.

Rishi Malhotra

Redwood Inference

Fyi on the product side —

We paused the quant rollout for a small cohort after telemetry surfaced a KV cache invalidation edge case that only shows up at long-sequence lengths used by DeltaHealth. The root cause is a kernel selection mismatch under a particular packing regime; the fix is narrow but requires a validation sweep across our long-seq test harness. Estimated timeline: 
- Patch submitted to main: ~2028-06-25
- Staging validation window: 2028-06-26 to 2028-06-28
- Customer staging validation + smoke: 2028-06-29 to 2028-07-02

I agree with keeping the accommodation timeboxed. My recommendation:
- Approve a staged commercial accommodation: 50% credit on committed baseline for 2 cycles, conditional on participation in the Early Access remediation plan (we provide dedicated test windows and an engineering liaison)
- Include a clause requiring DeltaHealth to accept an accelerated rollout checklist and to sign an acknowledgement that this is a one-time, remedial accommodation not a change to their committed price after the period

If Finance/Legal prefer rate adjustments vs credits, we can translate the credit into a 20% temporary committed-rate. Either way we need clear language tying the accommodation to milestone completion and to rollback protections.

Attachment: DH-impact-summary-June2028.pdf (contains telemetry snapshots and staging schedule)

—Laura
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sprint safeguard: pricing endorsement request for delayed quant rollout — proposed terms

Marissa / Rishi — looping Alex into the thread so procurement sees the proposal directly. Alex, thanks again for the details in the PDF — we pulled numbers with Rev Ops this morning and propose the following tidy option for approvals: 

Option A (credit): 50% credit on committed baseline for May and June invoices (applied as invoice credit).
Option B (rate): temporary committed rate of 20% off list for the two cycles May + June (billed at discounted rate).

Contingencies:
- Customer must sign the Early Access remediation agreement and acceptance checklist by 2028-06-20
- Product validation milestone (patch validated in staging + customer smoke) by 2028-07-02
- Accommodation automatically expires at the end of the second cycle unless extended by documented exec approval

We need a single executive to sign-off (commercial exec + finance acknowledgement). Can you advise, Marissa, whether you approve the approach and the specific numbers? If yes I’ll have Legal draft a compact amendment and Finance prepare the billing treatment.

Alex — if this is acceptable I’ll provide the amendment draft and target to get it back to you by EOD Tuesday.

Karthik

Subject: Re: Sprint safeguard: pricing endorsement request for delayed quant rollout — approval needed

Marissa —

Recommendation: approve Option A (50% credit on committed baseline for two cycles) with the contingencies listed below. Rationale: credit is cleaner for DeltaHealth procurement and can be documented as a one-time remedial accommodation; it also avoids rebilling complexity that could delay their PO. We limit precedent risk by making the credit strictly contingent on the Early Access acceptance and the clear milestone timeline.

Contingencies/controls I want called out in the amendment:
- Auto-expiry: accommodation ends after the two cycles unless explicitly extended by exec sign-off
- Acceptance clause: DeltaHealth must sign the Early Access remediation plan and accept rollback protections
- Accounting treatment: Finance to apply as invoice credit (no change to committed rate beyond the two cycles)
- Public-sector compliance: Legal to confirm wording meets procurement auditability needs

Please reply with Approve / Reject / Amend by EOD tomorrow so we can circulate the amendment to the customer. Alex — we’ll not proceed without explicit exec sign-off.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
